name: Tracelark
positioning: Tracelark turns traces, metrics and logs into one readable waterfall so engineering teams can find the slow span before their users do.
audience: Backend, platform and SRE engineers at product teams of 10 to 500 people who own services in production and carry the pager.
strategy: Win developer trust by speaking in the language of the terminal: real-looking traces, precise numbers and zero marketing fluff. Content teaches observability habits (reading the tail, slicing by route, alerting on budgets) so the brand earns attention as a field guide first and a product second.

designSystem.spacing: 8px base unit; sections breathe at 96-128px on desktop, 64px on mobile; 64px minimum safe margin on social canvases.
designSystem.radius: Small and technical: 6px on chips and bars, 12-20px on panels and windows, full pill on primary CTAs.
designSystem.borders: 1-2px hairlines in #1B2430 on #0D1117 panels; dashed hairlines for time axes and percentile markers.
designSystem.imagery: No photography. Product UI screens, trace waterfalls, terminal sessions and histograms drawn as inline SVG with illustrative sample data.
designSystem.shapes: Horizontal span bars, polyline sparklines, sine waveforms, concentric oscilloscope rings and a 40px blueprint grid.
designSystem.buttons: Primary: cyan pill with Void label in Inter 600. Secondary: transparent with 1px cyan outline. Mono command chips prefixed with a violet $.
designSystem.cards: Dark #0D1117 panels with a window chrome strip (three status dots: ember, violet, cyan) and mono headers.
designSystem.motifs: Trace waterfalls, latency sparklines, terminal windows, waveform signals; one ember-highlighted slow span per composition as the focal point.

artDirection: Every creative reads like a screenshot from a calm, well-instrumented production system: void background, blueprint grid, one glowing data object. Cyan carries the healthy signal, violet carries structure and secondary series, and ember is reserved for the single anomaly the eye should land on. Headlines are short Chakra Petch statements; supporting detail lives in Fira Code labels so the copy feels measured, not shouted. Sample data is always labelled illustrative and never claims real customer results.
